files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller’s checklist

Owner: H. Adeyemi. Complete in sequence; no skipping ahead.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July; some months all runs pay in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, supporting contracts, and the GL. If it has not been posted, book June prepaid amortization as ONE combined journal entry; do not duplicate an existing posting. Take a full month of amortization in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after first checking the GL to confirm it has not already been recorded.
5. Compare June vendor-bill documents with the GL, verify that each expense is coded to the correct account, and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Clearpath Partners LLC began in 2018 when a small group of former in-house operators decided that growing companies needed more than slide decks from their advisers. They built the firm around practical, hands-on help: clarifying operating plans, improving workflows, coordinating complex client projects, and giving leadership teams the structure to move decisions forward.

The company sells project-based consulting and managed business services to organizations that need experienced support without adding a permanent internal team. Engagements typically blend analysis, planning, facilitation, and implementation. Clearpath’s clients range from data-oriented businesses to professional-services and sustainability-focused firms, so the work is deliberately adaptable rather than tied to one industry.

The team has a distinctly working-session culture. Consultants are expected to arrive prepared, write clearly, and leave clients with usable tools rather than jargon. The operations staff keep schedules, vendors, billing, and project handoffs moving, while specialists join engagements when deeper accounting, marketing, or technical knowledge is required. Colleagues describe the atmosphere as low-ego, deadline-aware, and unusually fond of tidy checklists.

Clearpath Partners LLC is currently focused on delivering its active client work, sharpening its market positioning, and making routine internal processes more consistent. Leadership is also refining how the firm packages recurring services while preserving the tailored approach that built its reputation.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Position Clearpath Partners LLC as the practical partner for teams that need strategy translated into organized, usable action. The tone should remain direct, capable, and human—less consultancy theater, more experienced people getting the work moving.

## Priorities

- Complete the brand refresh, including message hierarchy, service descriptions, and a lighter visual system.
- Publish a steady mix of short field notes, client-friendly guides, and behind-the-scenes perspectives from the delivery team.
- Host two educational webinars per quarter, each built around a recurring operational problem rather than a broad thought-leadership theme.
- Pilot partner co-marketing with a complementary professional-services firm.
- Create reusable follow-up materials so webinar attendees and referrals receive a clear next step.

## Quarter focus

**Q3:** Finish core messaging, refresh priority web pages, prepare the webinar format, and recruit the first co-marketing partner.

**Q4:** Run the partner pilot, continue the webinar cadence, repurpose the strongest material, and review which topics generated useful conversations.

## Measures to watch

Track qualified inquiries, partner-sourced conversations, webinar attendance quality, content engagement, and movement from first conversation to scoped opportunity. Final channel choices remain subject to the Q2 close and leadership review.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from your chatty predecessor

H. Adeyemi — a few things I’d want someone to tell me before diving into the close:

- The bank tends to post its own fees and service charges near the end of the statement. That is normal here. We book those at close rather than recording them during the month.
- Please give the June vendor-bill coding a careful look. I was moving quickly, and one or two expenses may have landed in the wrong accounts. Treat the supporting documents in `bills/` as authoritative and reclass the GL where needed.
- The Q2 budget was locked early in April. As a result, the one-off items that arrived in June were never included in the plan; those unplanned items are the main reason the large variances will stand out.
- Payroll timing matters this month: the back half of June pays in early July. The payroll register contains the dates, so use it when preparing the accrual.
